target.projectDescription: OpenAdapt 0.1.0 (pyproject.toml [tool.poetry]) - 'GUI Process Automation with Transformers': a desktop app that records GUI activity (screenshots, keyboard/mouse ActionEvents, WindowEvents) into a local SQLite database via SQLAlchemy 1.4.43 ORM/Core, replays them with strategies (NaiveReplayStrategy, StatefulReplayStrategy, ...), scrubs PII/PHI with presidio, and offers a nicegui 1.2.16 native desktop UI (openadapt/app) for recording, DB import/export (bz2-compressed SQLite files) and visualization. Alembic 1.8.1 manages the schema; python-fire 0.4.0 provides the CLI (record/replay/share/scrub/utils entry points). The audit target is the data access layer (openadapt/crud.py, openadapt/db.py, openadapt/models.py), the app UI (openadapt/app), the recorders (openadapt/record.py, events.py) and the CLI entry points.

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: OpenAdapt is a local desktop application, so input boundaries are UI events, CLI arguments, files and configuration - there is NO HTTP/API request surface in the analyzed code (recorded as not observed). The trust-relevant boundaries are: (1) the nicegui recording-name prompt - ui.input (openadapt/app/cards.py:44-49) captures free text; the entered name is concatenated into a shell command `Popen("python3 -m openadapt.record " + name, shell=True)` (cards.py:76-79) which spawns the record CLI, whose fire-registered record(task_description) parameter (openadapt/record.py:507-508) stores the text as Recording.task_description in the DB via create_recording -> crud.insert_recording (parameterized ORM insert); (2) the nicegui import dialog - LocalFilePicker returns a user-chosen file path (cards.py:21-24, local_file_picker.py:87-91 msg["args"]["data"]["path"]) and on_import(selected_file) (openadapt/app/util.py:20-28) bz2-decompresses that file over openadapt.db, which makes the ENTIRE database content (including recording.platform and recording.task_description) attacker-controllable through an imported file; (3) the fire CLI - record/replay/share/send/receive entry points take task_description/strategy_name/timestamp/recording_id/wormhole_code (record.py:507, replay.py:20, share.py:70/86); `python -m openadapt.share send --recording_id=N` drives the export chain that reaches raw SQL execution; dynamic fire.Fire(get_functions(__name__)) registrations (scrub.py:281, utils.py:508/525) expose every public function of those modules as CLI commands (not statically resolvable); (4) files - open() (config .env reads in config.py:37, crud.py:167/:170 env-file rewrite, app/main.py:30 logo, app/build.py:23 spec, app/util.py:21/:36 db files) and bz2.BZ2File (app/util.py:22/:37, the DB import/export channel); (5) environment/config - os.getenv (config.py:146), python-dotenv load_dotenv/find_dotenv (config.py:23-24), read_env_file (config.py:27-47) and ~42 config.<ATTR> reads (operator-level trust: DB_URL, DB_FNAME, SCRUB_*, OPENAI_API_KEY consumed across the package); (6) the database itself - recordings read back via ORM (get_recording_by_id, get_latest_recording, _get) expose DB-derived values (recording.platform, recording.task_description etc.) whose reads are concentrated in crud.py:142 (inside the raw-SQL f-string), record.py:521, utils.py:309-370, visualize.py:149/248-249. The dominant SQL execution channels are exactly two: db.execute(sa.insert(table), to_insert) (crud.py:48, SQLAlchemy Core parameterized insert used by the event writers) and connection.execute(sql) (crud.py:180, engine.begin() over a RAW SQL STRING built by export_sql's f-string at crud.py:142 from DB-derived recording values - the injection-shaped channel). The ORM chains db.query(...).filter(...)/.order_by(...)/.filter_by(...) (crud.py:103-246) and db.add/commit/refresh (crud.py:112-114) compile to parameterized SQL and are not raw-SQL sinks.

Whether these origins constitute a realistic attacker boundary for a local desktop app is a labeling/triage decision - the chain is recorded as a candidate, not presumed vulnerable. The Core insert path (crud.py:48) is parameterized. No HTTP request path exists in the analyzed code.

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs; in this project NO row is expected to resolve at API level: the only SQL APIs (sa.insert, Session/Connection execute) live in the sqlalchemy library which is NOT part of the CodeQL database, so import chains cannot resolve to library modules; nicegui widgets (ui.input) and fire.Fire are likewise external library calls with no in-snapshot module. The column is kept for cross-project contract consistency.
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic receiver, name conventions). The execute-member matching is receiver-name-agnostic (any <obj>.execute(...) matches): both observed sites are SQLAlchemy execute calls (db = Session() at crud.py:23, connection from engine.begin() at crud.py:179), but the query cannot prove receiver identity; name-collision noise is possible and is left to the labeling step.

extraction.expectedVolume: roughly 100-125 source rows (ui_input 3, ui_event 1, cli: 8 fire.Fire rows + 5 registered-function parameter rows + 1 Popen row, file ~14, db_read ~19, config ~44, env 3, internal_transfer 14: four _insert call sites x 3 positional args + one create_db call site x 2) and roughly 9-12 sink rows (2 execute sql_text rows, 1 bound_params row, ~4 construction rows - the crud.py:142 f-string via the sql-variable assignment shape plus 3 non-SQL f-strings inside create_db caught by the inside-SQL-function shape, 2 internal_sql_wrapper rows, 1 sql_object_construction row). Tiny volumes are expected and honest: this is a ~4.9k LOC application with exactly two SQL execution call sites, in line with the task contract that absent families are recorded rather than fabricated.

uncoveredCases: Dynamic fire registrations: fire.Fire(utils.get_functions(__name__)) (scrub.py:281) and fire.Fire(get_functions(__name__)) (utils.py:508, 525) expose every public function of those modules as CLI commands at runtime (inspect.getmembers over sys.modules); their targets cannot be resolved statically, so their parameters are NOT emitted as cli rows. Only the fire.Fire call nodes themselves are emitted.

No HTTP/API request boundary exists in the analyzed code: nicegui runs in native desktop mode and its FastAPI/Socket.IO server internals live in the nicegui library, which is not part of the CodeQL database. UI event handler closures (on_change=lambda e: ...) and their lambda parameters are not modeled directly; the ui.input widget call node is the emitted boundary instead.

UI label/checkbox value reads (selected_file.text, delete.value in cards.py:32) are not emitted as separate families: selected_file.text is the import file path (path-shaped, Pass-1 relevance) and delete.value is a boolean flag; the file content itself enters via the file family (open/bz2.BZ2File/copyfileobj).

Name-based matching caveats: fireRegisteredFunction resolves registered functions by bare name (record/replay/send_recording/receive_recording are unique module-level names in this snapshot, so no false positives here, but the shape is name-based); db_read rows match any <obj named recording>.<column-name> attribute read regardless of the object's actual origin (strategy constructors also receive a `recording` parameter); internal SQL wrapper resolution (callsSqlWrapper) is name-only and subject to dynamic dispatch ambiguity.

export_sql is NOT an internal SQL wrapper (its body builds the string but does not execute it): the export_sql(recording_id) call at crud.py:208 is not an internal_transfer row, and cross-function value flow (export_sql's return -> local sql -> create_db argument 1 -> connection.execute) is not traced at extraction time; the chain is instead covered by the db_read rows at crud.py:142 (inputs), the sql_fstring construction row (the string), the create_db internal_sql_wrapper row and the create_db argument-1 transfer row at crud.py:209 (the hand-off), and the sql_text row at crud.py:180 (the execution).

The construction family's inside-SQL-function condition (b) intentionally also captures non-SQL f-strings located inside functions that directly execute SQL (create_db's f"recording_{recording_id}.db", f"{config.ENV_FILE_PATH}-{t}", f"DB_FNAME={db_fname}\n" at crud.py:161/164/169) - these are filename/env-line constructions, expected as candidate noise for the labeling step to reject; %-format/.format/concat construction subshapes exist in the query but produce no rows in this snapshot (no such sites observed).
Keyword-argument hand-offs into SQL wrapper functions are not captured by internal_transfer (positional arguments only, positions 0-9).

API-level (ApiGraphs) resolution is not attempted: sqlalchemy, nicegui, fire, bz2 and dotenv are external libraries not included in the CodeQL database, so no row can resolve at API level; all rows are match_kind 'ast'.

The ORM query chains (db.query/filter/order_by/add/commit/refresh) and the alembic ops tree are not extracted as sinks (parameterized/compiled channels); sqlalchemy Session.execute/Connection.execute definitions live in the external library and cannot be extracted as sql_api_def rows - this project has no project-defined raw-SQL API definitions.
